name: The Stonewall Fig of Ka Wai Man Road

location.address: Ka Wai Man Road Garden, Kennedy Town

access: Free, public garden, viewable at any time
transport: Short walk from MTR Kennedy Town station Exit C, one street over from the Forbes Street stone wall trees (hkg_002)
verify_notes: The single most singular candidate this pass, exactly the kind of tree the brief flagged as worth prioritising: Hong Kong's government Old and Valuable Trees register lists this specimen under BOTH designations at once, ref ARCHSD CW/9, type field literally 'OVT & SWT' (Old and Valuable Tree AND Stonewall Tree), dbh 1800mm (1.8m trunk diameter), height 17m, crown spread 24m, and its condition notes explicitly include the word 'Stonewall' alongside three separate lean observations (natural phototropism, response growth, self-corrected), the classic signature of a tree that has spent decades growing out of and around a masonry retaining wall rather than open ground. Last inspected 17/3/2023, department Architectural Services Department (the department responsible for government stonewall structures, not the Leisure and Cultural Services Department that runs most park trees, itself a small clue the tree grows on built structure rather than parkland soil). It sits only 111m from the already-published Forbes Street wall (hkg_002), a two-minute walk on the same Kennedy Town hillside, so it extends rather than duplicates that walk. FLAG FOR THE WRITER: this pass found no independent narrative second source specifically naming Ka Wai Man Road Garden (unlike Forbes Street, which has a Conservancy Association campaign page and a dedicated heritage site); general Kennedy Town stone wall context comes from Forbes Street coverage rather than this specific site, so this ships as a single-detailed-source (government register) entry, flagged accordingly. Also flag an access caveat worth a recheck: Ka Wai Man Road is the site of an active CEDD public housing redevelopment (construction began 31 Oct 2022, phased across the Ex-Police Married Officers Quarters and Ex-Mount Davis Cottage Area sites nearby), but the register's own last-inspection date of March 2023 postdates that start, which per this project's own reading of register data is meaningful evidence the tree was still standing after work began, not proof of its status today. A future pass should sanity-check the garden itself has not been absorbed into the construction site before this ships to a live page. No photo hunted this pass per the brief (verification only).

name: The Banyan of King George V Park

location.address: King George V Memorial Park, Canton Road, Jordan, Kowloon

transport: Short walk from MTR Jordan station, or from the northern end of Kowloon Park via Canton Road
verify_notes: Government Old and Valuable Trees register, ref LCSD YTM/98, 'King George V Memorial Park, Kowloon', dbh 1800mm, height 13m, crown spread 18m, last inspected 17/11/2022, tree vigor normal, overall risk rating low. Only 156m from the already-published King Banyan of Kowloon Park (hkg_001), effectively the same neighbourhood walk continued a couple of minutes further. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION for the writer: Hong Kong has TWO parks named after King George V. This one is in Jordan, Kowloon, beside Canton Road, opened 11 June 1941 (delayed opening because the governor was ill), damaged and used as a rubbish dump during the Japanese occupation, rebuilt by the Urban Council with three Chinese-styled kiosks and reopened 21 March 1954, expanded westward in the 1970s after Canton Road was realigned, and redesigned again in the 1990s following the Airport Core Programme land reclamation, corroborated by Wikipedia's dedicated article on this specific park. The OTHER King George V Memorial Park is on Hong Kong Island in Sai Ying Pun, unrelated, built on the site of a former hospital garden with its own well-documented stone wall trees; do not conflate the two parks or their histories. Wikipedia's history of the Kowloon park does not name this individual tree, so the entry is register-plus-general-park-history rather than a narrative confirmed specifically for this tree; flagged accordingly. No photo hunted this pass per the brief.

name: The Camphor of Kowloon Park Drive

location.address: Kowloon Park Drive Children's Playground, Kowloon Park, Tsim Sha Tsui

transport: 10-15 min walk from MTR Tsim Sha Tsui station, within Kowloon Park via Kowloon Park Drive, at the southern end of the park from the King Banyan (hkg_001)
verify_notes: Government Old and Valuable Trees register, ref ARCHSD YTM/12, 'Kowloon Park Drive Children's Playground', dbh 2000mm (2m trunk diameter, larger than the two camphors already published in this city file, hkg_004 at She Shan and hkg_006 at Lai Chi Wo, though those are New Territories village feng shui trees while this one is an urban park specimen, a different context worth keeping distinct in the story), height 16m, crown spread 20m, last inspected 6/10/2022, tree vigor normal. 703m from the King Banyan (hkg_001), a 10-minute walk within the same park, at the opposite southern end near the children's playground and aviary section of Kowloon Park. Chosen specifically to give the Hong Kong page a camphor within easy reach of its Kowloon Park cluster, rather than only the remote New Territories village camphors already on the page: a reader who has just seen the 400-year banyan can walk to this one in the same visit. A second, smaller camphor (ref ARCHSD YTM/13, dbh 1350mm) stands in the same playground; this pass selected the larger, more established of the two. No independent narrative source found for this specific specimen beyond the government register itself; ships single-source, flagged. No photo hunted this pass per the brief.

name: The Banyan of Nathan Road

location.address: Park Lane Shopper's Boulevard, Nathan Road, opposite St Andrew's Church, Tsim Sha Tsui

access: Free, public street, viewable at any time
transport: A few minutes' walk from MTR Tsim Sha Tsui station Exit A1, on Nathan Road's Park Lane Shopper's Boulevard stretch
verify_notes: Government Old and Valuable Trees register, ref LCSD YTM/6, dbh 2070mm, height 19m, crown spread 22m, last inspected 3/10/2022, tree vigor normal, overall tree risk rating moderate (compacted soil, cable/brace support, restriction within dripline over 75 percent, all typical of a mature street tree hemmed in by a busy shopping boulevard rather than a sign of decline). 502m from the King Banyan of Kowloon Park (hkg_001), a 6-7 minute walk, so it extends that same visit onto Hong Kong's most famous shopping street. The register locates it directly opposite St Andrew's Church, Kowloon's oldest Anglican and English-speaking Protestant church, built 1904-06 in Victorian Gothic style on a small hill on Nathan Road, a gift to the community from Sir Paul Chater (the Armenian businessman and co-founder of Hong Kong Land), a Grade I/II historic building per Wikipedia's article on the church, giving the tree a genuinely photogenic pairing (a banyan against Victorian Gothic stonework on the Golden Mile). General colour on Tsim Sha Tsui's street banyans as a 'reminder of the days when all Tsim Sha Tsui streets were lined with similar trees' found in passing search results but not tied to this specific tree by name, so treated as background rather than a confirmed fact about this individual; the register itself remains the primary source for this tree's own existence and measurements, flagged as single-source-for-specifics accordingly. No photo hunted this pass per the brief.
